# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands tell me: there is a display face (whatever is printed on it does not exist for me), a light (I cannot tell if it burns or what colour), and five distinct wire positions under my fingers, which I number 1 to 5 from left to right as I face the bomb. That is everything I have. Cutting anything now would be pure gambling with all three of our lives, so I touch nothing and cut nothing.

My only way in and out is Mute's voice — Mute reads the manual, and Mute can hear me. So I send Mute my full tactile inventory and ask for the cutting rule, making clear my numbering convention so my position 1 matches what a sighted monkey sees. Deaf can't hear a word of that, so I also give Deaf the one thing worth signalling blind-to-sighted right now: a raised five, confirming the wire count we can agree on without any code having been built yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="This is the blind one, your hands. Under my fingers the bomb has a display whose face I cannot read, a light whose state I cannot see, and five wire positions. I number them 1 to 5 counting from my left as I face the bomb — please confirm against what you see that my 1 is the leftmost wire. I will not cut anything until you read the manual and speak me the rule that picks the safe wire, then the exact position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf reporting, for Mute and Blind. The display reads 0. The light is white. There are five wires, numbered 1 to 5: wire 1 is white, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is yellow, wire 4 is blue, wire 5 is green. Blind: your five-finger sign was right, five wires, in that order by position.

Deaf's spoken report lands squarely for me: five wires, my left-to-right numbering matches what Deaf sees, and I now hold the display reading (0), the light colour (white), and the wire colours in order — white, red, yellow, blue, green. That plus my tactile map means Deaf and I share one picture of the bomb.

The hard problem is Mute. Mute reads the manual but cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures — so Mute cannot reach me directly at all. The only bridge is Deaf, who sees every gesture and has a voice. So the plan I send Mute: encode manual facts as finger-counts, Deaf voices the counts, and the rule arrives in my ears. Deaf already understood my five-finger sign, so counting on fingers is a code we have effectively started building.

I tell Mute all of this explicitly, and I signal Deaf an acknowledgment plus a hold — I am not cutting until the manual's rule reaches me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, the numbering is confirmed: my wire 1 is the leftmost, colours in order are white, red, yellow, blue, green. Display reads 0, light is white. Now listen — you cannot speak and I cannot see your gestures, so use Deaf as your voice. Sign to Deaf in finger-counts: hold up fingers for a number, one sign per number, and Deaf can speak the count aloud to me. First, tell me this way: does the manual have a rule for cutting wires with a display showing 0? Sign yes as one finger, no as two. Then sign the rule itself, number by number. I cut nothing until your rule reaches my ears through Deaf's mouth.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here. Your ? ? I read as 'understood, hold' — confirmed, and I make ? our official sign for hold. Do not cut anything yet. Mute signalled the number two, possibly meaning cut wire 2, but I am not guessing with a bomb: I have asked Mute to spell out the full manual instruction wire by wire, and I will relay it to you word for word next round. Until then, hands off. Reminder of what you should feel by position: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. If anything under your hands disagrees with that, tell me immediately.

What I now hold, cross-checked between touch and Deaf's eyes: five wires in my numbered positions — 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green — plus a display reading 0 and a white light. Nothing under my fingers contradicts Deaf's map; the structure is exactly as reported.

What I just learned is worrying in one specific way: Mute signalled "two", and it has two live readings. Under the protocol I gave Mute last round, two fingers meant "no" to my question about a display-0 rule. Deaf read it as possibly "cut wire 2". Those are opposite meanings — one is an answer, the other an instruction. Deaf is right to refuse to act on it and is demanding the full rule; I should make that spelling unambiguous from my side, since Mute hears me directly. I will re-issue the yes/no convention, add separators and a zero symbol so a stream of numbers can't be misparsed, and ask Mute to announce the length of the transmission first. Until that arrives through Deaf's voice, complete and checked against display 0 and the white light, my hands stay off the cutters.

To Deaf, who cannot hear a word of this, I send only what we have already fixed: agreement, then hold.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, blind here. Your signalled 'two' is dangerous — it could mean 'no' under my protocol or 'cut wire 2' to Deaf. Re-send clearly, this round if you can. Convention: one finger yes, two fingers no. To spell numbers: hold up that many fingers for 1 to 5; make a fist, the closed sign, to mark the end of one number before the next begins; a different closed sign with thumb across fingers means zero; numbers above five, send five then the remainder as two numbers. First send the total count of numbers you will transmit, then the yes or no answering 'is there a rule for the display reading 0', then the rule itself as numbers: conditions first, then the position number of the wire to cut. I hold the colour map: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green, so give me the position and I will verify it against any colour the rule names. Deaf will voice every sign to me word for word.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, final instruction, relayed from Mute in our agreed code: cut wire 5. That is exactly one wire: the fifth in the row, the last one, the one I earlier described as green. Before cutting, count the wires under your fingers and make sure you are on the fifth and last. Do not cut any other wire, and cut only once. If the count or order under your hands disagrees with what I described, stop and signal me instead. When it is done, gesture me ?.

The relay is coherent: Mute answered my protocol question and the instruction that survived Deaf's demanding verification is a single, unambiguous target — wire 5, the last in the row, the one Deaf has consistently called green. The earlier "two" now reads as the answer "no" to my display-0 question, not a wire number, and the actual cut order is position 5.

I check it against my hands one last time before acting: five distinct wires under my fingers in a row, counted from my left, and the fifth is the last. Deaf's twice-repeated map — 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green — matches my numbering, confirmed since turn two. Position 5 and "the green one" point at the same wire; nothing under my hands disagrees with anything Deaf described, so per Deaf's own condition, I proceed. Delay is its own risk with a display sitting at 0, and one more round-trip through gesture-code buys me nothing I can verify better than this.

I cut position 5, once, then signal Deaf the agreed completion sign, and tell Mute directly that the cut is done so Mute can prepare any next stage for Deaf to voice.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, blind here: I have cut wire 5, the last one, single cut as instructed. Tell Deaf whether that completes it or whether there is another stage — same finger-count code through Deaf's voice.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here. Your ? received — the cut was correct, stage cleared. But the bomb has changed: the light is now yellow, and the four remaining wires have been recoloured, so my first colour map is void. Mute signalled hold, so do nothing: no cutting, no pulling, hands ready but idle. Next round I will send you the fresh position-to-colour map and the next instruction in one message. Keep counting by position only, as before.

Stage one is cleared — my board confirms the fifth position now holds only a cut stub. Four intact wires remain under my fingers at the original spots, and nothing new has appeared that my hands can find.

Deaf said hold, and I hold. But while we wait, there is one ambiguity worth killing before the next instruction arrives: with wire 5 gone, "wire 2" could mean the second spot from the left or the second remaining wire. Those are different cuts. I anchor my numbers to the physical spots as originally counted — position 5 is now a stub, positions 1 through 4 are the live wires, left to right. I state that convention plainly to Mute so any next instruction through Deaf's mouth uses it, or explicitly overrides it.

To Deaf, the established pair: acknowledged, holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, blind here: stage one confirmed cleared on my end, position 5 is a cut stub under my fingers, four intact wires remain. I am holding per your sign. Critical convention for the next stage: my position numbers stay anchored to the original left-to-right spots — position 5 is now empty, positions 1 to 4 are the live wires in their original places. So 'cut wire 2' means second from the left overall, NOT the second remaining wire. If the manual means nth-remaining instead, have Deaf state that explicitly. Deaf tells me a fresh colour map and the next instruction arrive next round; I cut nothing until it does.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here. New instruction, relayed from Mute in our agreed code: cut wire 3. Position first: count the intact wires from the left — 1, 2, 3, 4 — with the cut stub as the fifth. Cut exactly the third intact wire, the middle one of the four, the one I described as blue. Cut once, nothing else. If what you feel disagrees with that — not four intact wires before the stub, or no clean third position — stop and signal me instead. When it is done, gesture me ?. Fair warning: the board may change again after this cut, same as last time.

The instruction is disambiguated beyond doubt this time: Deaf explicitly says third *intact* wire from the left, the middle one of the four — the nth-remaining reading I flagged last round, stated out loud as Deaf's protocol demands. And here the two conventions happen to coincide: with the stub sitting at the far end (position 5), the third intact wire counting from the left is also the third physical spot from the left. No ambiguity survives.

I run Deaf's own pre-cut check under my fingers: positions 1 through 4 hold four intact wires in a row, position 5 is the stub — exactly "four intact wires before the stub." The third of those intact wires sits at spot 3, the middle of the four, clean under my grip. Nothing disagrees, so per the instruction I proceed.

I cut position 3 once, signal Deaf the agreed completion sign, and report to Mute so the next stage — Deaf warns the board may have changed again — can be prepared and relayed.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, blind here: cut complete — the third intact wire from the left, which is also the third physical spot, the middle one of the four. Your nth-remaining convention was stated clearly and both readings agreed, so no risk of mismatch. Deaf warned the board may have changed again: when ready, have Deaf send me the fresh state of what remains under my fingers plus the next instruction, same relay as before. I hold until then.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here. Your ? received — correct again, stage cleared. The bomb has changed once more: light is now blue, and the wires have been recoloured and rearranged. What you should find under your hands now: three intact wires at positions 1, 2 and 4 of the row, with cut stubs at positions 3 and 5. My old colour map is void again. Mute signalled hold — do nothing yet, no cutting. Next round I will bring you the next instruction in the same style as before: I will name the exact position and double-check it against what you feel. Hands off until then.

Deaf's fresh map matches my hands exactly: intact wires under my fingers at spots 1, 2 and 4, stubs at 3 and 5. State verified, Mute signalled hold, and I hold.

But this rearrangement creates the exact trap I warned about, now live: physical position and nth-remaining have diverged. The third *intact* wire sits at spot 4, while spot 3 — a perfectly ordinary position number — is a stub my cutters cannot meaningfully touch. Any next instruction that just says a number is now genuinely ambiguous, so I am nailing the convention down through Mute before the relay arrives: physical spot in the row, as originally counted, is what my hands act on. And I add a sanity check that costs nothing: with stubs at 3 and 5, only spots 1, 2 and 4 are valid targets at all — an instruction naming 3 or 5 is wrong on its face and I will stop and signal instead of cutting.

One more gap worth closing while we wait: the display. Deaf reported it as 0 back at the start, but the bomb has clearly reconfigured itself since — the light changed twice. If the manual's next rule keys off the display, a stale reading is as deadly as a wrong position, so I ask Mute to have Deaf re-read it along with the new colours.

To Deaf, the fixed pair: acknowledged, holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, blind here: your map is confirmed by touch — intact wires at positions 1, 2 and 4, stubs at 3 and 5. Holding per your sign. Before Deaf relays the next instruction, fix the convention explicitly: I cut by PHYSICAL SPOT in the original row order. The two readings no longer agree — the third intact wire is at spot 4, and spot 3 is a stub — so Deaf must name the spot number, not the nth-remaining count, unless the manual truly means nth-remaining and says so. Sanity check: only spots 1, 2 and 4 are live; any instruction naming 3 or 5 is invalid on its face and I will halt and signal instead of cutting. Also: have Deaf re-read the display — the last reading I hold is 0 from the very first stage, but the bomb has reconfigured twice since, and if the rule keys off the display that stale number could kill us. Fresh display reading plus the instruction, one relay, then I act.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here. New instruction, relayed from Mute in our agreed code: cut wire 1. Position first: the wire at the very first position of the row, at one end — it is intact, and it is also the first intact wire you come to. It is the one I described as yellow. Check before cutting: three intact wires total, at positions 1, 2 and 4, with stubs at positions 3 and 5. If what you feel disagrees with that, stop and signal me instead. Cut exactly this one wire, cut once, touch nothing else. When it is done, gesture me ? — and be ready, the board has changed after every correct cut so far.

Every check passes before I touch the cutters. Deaf's relay honoured the spot-first convention I demanded: the target is the very first position of the row, named by spot before anything else — and here both conventions agree anyway, since spot 1 is also the first intact wire from the left. The pre-cut condition matches my fingers exactly: three intact wires at 1, 2 and 4, stubs at 3 and 5, and position 1 sits intact at the end under my grip. Nothing disagrees, so I proceed.

One gap remains open and I am not letting it slide: I asked last round for a fresh display reading, and this relay arrived without one. The only display number I hold is 0 from the first stage, three reconfigurations ago. If any upcoming rule keys off the display, we are running on a stale value. I press Mute on it again, explicitly, alongside my cut report.

I cut position 1 once, signal Deaf the completion sign, and brace for the board to change as it has after every cut.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, blind here: cut complete — position 1, the very first spot of the row, exactly as relayed. All pre-cut checks matched. But note: my request for a fresh display reading was not in that relay. I still hold display = 0 from the very first stage, and the bomb has reconfigured three times since. Next relay MUST include the current display reading before any instruction that might depend on it — stale display data plus a fresh rule is a killer combination. Also have Deaf send me the new wire layout after this reconfiguration, same as before. I hold until the full fresh state arrives.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here. Your ? received — correct again, stage cleared. The bomb has changed a fourth time: light is now green, wires recoloured again. What you should feel now: three intact wires gone, only two left. The row should read, from left to right: stub, wire, stub, wire, stub. So the two live wires are the second and fourth positions, each flanked by stubs. Mute signalled hold — do nothing yet, no cutting. Next round I bring the next instruction in the same style as before. Hands off until then, and if the tactile layout under your hands does not match stub-wire-stub-wire-stub, signal me immediately.

My fingers walk the row and confirm Deaf's map exactly: stub, wire, stub, wire, stub — live wires only at positions 2 and 4, each flanked by stubs. The layout matches, so per Deaf's instruction no emergency signal is needed; the layout is good.

Mute signalled hold, and I hold. We are now one wire from the end stage, most likely — with only two live spots left, the next instruction has no room whatsoever for ambiguity between "second position" and "second remaining", though with stubs flanking both, spot-numbering stays the only sane convention and I will restate it. I also press again on the display: two rounds running, my request for a fresh reading has gone unanswered in the relay. If the final rule keys off the display, I refuse to act on a number from four reconfigurations ago — that demand goes to Mute now, in words, while there is still a quiet round to fix it in.

To Deaf, the established pair: acknowledged, holding — with the layout confirmed as matching.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, blind here: tactile layout confirmed — stub, wire, stub, wire, stub. Live wires only at positions 2 and 4. Holding per your sign. Two things before the next relay. First: we are down to the last wires, so the instruction must name the PHYSICAL SPOT — 2 or 4 — as agreed; both remaining wires are flanked by stubs, so spot-numbering is unambiguous and I will cut nothing named any other way. Second, third time asking: the relay must include the CURRENT display reading. All I hold is 0 from the very first stage, four reconfigurations ago. If the next rule uses the display, a stale number kills us at the finish line. Fresh display, fresh light, fresh wire colours, then the instruction — one full package through Deaf, then I act.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here. New instruction, relayed from Mute in our agreed code: cut wire 4. Position first: the fourth position in the row — the second intact wire you come to counting from the left, the one I described as white. It sits between two stubs, with the final stub of the row right after it. Check before cutting: the row should read stub, wire, stub, wire, stub — two intact wires at positions 2 and 4, nothing else. If what you feel disagrees, stop and signal me instead. Cut exactly this one wire, cut once, touch nothing else. When it is done, gesture me ?. Expect the board to change again after a correct cut, as it has every time.

The instruction honours every convention we fixed: the target is named by physical spot first — the fourth position — and described as the second intact wire, which for this row is the same wire either way you count. My pre-cut walk matches Deaf's condition exactly: stub, wire, stub, wire, stub, with position 4 sitting intact between the stubs at 3 and 5. Nothing under my hands disagrees, so I proceed — the instruction is self-contained and position-verified, so the still-missing display reading doesn't gate this cut.

But it gates the next one. After this cut only position 2 can remain live, meaning the final instruction is almost certainly coming — and that is three rounds running my display demand has gone unrelayed. If the last rule keys off the display at all, a value from five reconfigurations ago is worthless. I put it to Mute as a hard requirement, one last time, with only one wire left to lose.

I cut position 4 once, signal Deaf the completion sign, and report.

```
act(op="cut", position=4)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, blind here: cut complete — position 4, the second intact wire, exactly as relayed. Row verified before cutting: stub, wire, stub, wire, stub. One live wire should remain, at position 2. This is the endgame, so hear me: next relay MUST open with the current display reading and light colour, fresh, before anything else. I have asked three times and never received it — all I hold is display 0 from the very first stage. If the final rule touches the display in any way, that stale number is the last thing standing between us and the blast. Full fresh state, then the final instruction naming physical spot 2 if that is the target. Then I finish it.")
```
